title: Frame
description: A player's mech, as a PC-grade character sheet (see common/sf2e-common.schema.json#/$defs/pcStatblock). REWORKED 2026-09-20 for the lockstep model; every level-12 and Resonance assumption from the previous version is gone. A Frame does NOT replace its pilot's own character sheet — it AMPLIFIES it, contributing hardness and high AC (the properties that make Frame-scale combat survivable) and extending what the pilot can already do, so a spellcaster's magic reaches across huge distances rather than becoming a different spell list. Level is LOCKSTEP with the pilot: one shared level, starting at 1, advancing on milestone XP at the same moment the pilot advances — never independently, never drifting. Progression is bought with a credit BUDGET spent on the machine's own feats, weapons, armour and equipment, exactly like kitting out a PC; it never buys levels. Every Frame starts with a loadout mirroring the job the machine was actually built for, and how that tool behaves when used in a fight — a crane rig plays like a reach weapon at city scale. SF2E's own vehicle rules are deliberately NOT used (open-questions.json#vehicle-and-frame-rules-model). Vehicles use this same shape and sit alongside Frames as an equal track: Frames are slow, tough and near-blind; vehicles are fast, fragile, carry up to three, and some of them see extremely well. One file per Frame in data/characters/frames/.

pilotKidRef.description: id of the kid who pilots this Frame.

generation.description: Gen 1 is the classic century-and-a-half-old utility fleet the party starts on — converted diggers, cranes, disaster-response rigs — reverse-engineered from a single fragment and flyable by anyone. Gen 2 is built from genuinely recovered ship material, DNA-gated, and arrives MUCH later (roughly level 4 at the earliest). See quarantine/ideas/story/dossier-second-generation-frames.md.

level.description: LOCKSTEP with the pilot's own level. Starts at 1. Advances on milestone XP at the same time every other pilot, Frame and vehicle in the party advances — there is no independent Frame level, no drift cap, and no per-machine XP. See open-questions.json#frame-scale-starting-level and #levelling-and-request-fulfilment.

utilityRole.description: The job this machine was actually built to do — lifting, digging, demolition, disaster response, recon. Drives the starting loadout: the initial kit should mirror this job and how that tool behaves when it is used in a fight.

concept.description: One or two sentences on how this machine reads in play, and what its pilot's own abilities look like once amplified to Frame scale.

loadout.description: The machine's own weapons, armour, gear and consumables — bought with the pilot's credit budget, exactly like kitting out a PC. This replaces the old Resonance-gated abilityBands, which are deleted.

kind.description: feat covers the machine's own Frame feats, which work like PC feats.

permanence.description: permanent kit stays; consumable is spent; renewable is restocked between operations.

usageLimit.description: For permanent kit carrying an activated ability.

startingKit.description: True if this came with the machine as part of its utility-role loadout rather than being bought.

vision.description: Sight is a real mechanical axis, not flavour — see ideas/entries/vision-as-chassis-axis.json and foundry-vision-restricted-spotting.json, both accepted. Frames are near-blind giants; armour costs vision. Long-ranged weapons need somebody else close enough to actually see the target, which is what makes recon chassis matter.

range.description: Effective sight range, in the campaign's own map units.

stealth.description: How well this chassis avoids being seen. Recon vehicles are excellent at this; helicopters are deliberately terrible at it despite seeing well themselves.

canSpotForOthers.description: Whether this chassis can mark targets for teammates who cannot see them.

damageState.description: Frame HP is a campaign resource, not an encounter resource — machines do not heal between fights, they move down this track and are repaired. See config.json#frameEconomy.

syncedPilotRefs.description: Gen 2 only. Pilots who have already taken Frame Sickness in THIS machine and cleared it. A pilot not on this list takes Slowed 1 for their entire first fight in it — a one-time, per-machine cost that exists to make adopting one Frame better than hopping between them, and which players are warned about in advance. See open-questions.json#gen2-sync-duration-mechanism.
